dataset.provenance_note: The CSV was supplied without documentation of its source or measurement units. Units are therefore not shown, and the data should not be assumed to represent real-world weather observations until verified.

classification.selection_metric: Mean 5-fold cross-validated F1-score of the 'rain' class (training data only)
classification.selection_rule: Highest mean CV F1 for the 'rain' class; if the simpler Logistic Regression is within one standard error of the best, prefer it. The test set is NOT used for this choice.
classification.selection_reason: Random Forest Classifier beat Logistic Regression by 0.3255 in mean cross-validated F1, more than one standard error (0.0018), so the extra complexity is justified.

audit.tree_rules:
|--- Humidity <= 70.1
|   |--- class: no rain
|--- Humidity >  70.1
|   |--- Cloud_Cover <= 49.9
|   |   |--- class: no rain
|   |--- Cloud_Cover >  49.9
|   |   |--- Temperature <= 24.9
|   |   |   |--- class: rain
|   |   |--- Temperature >  24.9
|   |   |   |--- class: no rain

logistic_regression.name: Logistic Regression
logistic_regression.description: Linear model of the log-odds of rain. Features are standardised inside the pipeline (scaler fitted on training folds only). class_weight='balanced' gives the rare 'rain' class more weight during training.

random_forest.name: Random Forest Classifier
random_forest.description: Ensemble of decision trees trained on bootstrap samples; can learn non-linear threshold rules and feature interactions. Trees do not need feature scaling. class_weight='balanced' counters the class imbalance.

regression.selection_rule: Lowest mean CV RMSE; if the simpler Multiple Linear Regression is within one standard error of the best, prefer it. The test set is NOT used for this choice.
regression.selection_reason: Multiple Linear Regression had the best mean cross-validated RMSE.
regression.output_policy: Evaluation metrics use the raw, unclipped model outputs. On the prediction page the value shown is limited to the 0–100 scale of the target column, and the raw model output is always shown next to it whenever limiting was applied.

linear_regression.name: Multiple Linear Regression
linear_regression.description: Fits Cloud_Cover = b0 + b1·Temperature + b2·Humidity + b3·Wind_Speed + b4·Pressure by ordinary least squares. It is the linear baseline: easy to interpret, but it can only capture straight-line (additive) relationships.

random_forest.name: Random Forest Regressor
random_forest.description: Averages many regression trees, so it can model non-linear relationships and interactions between features without them being specified by hand. More flexible, but also more prone to fitting noise.
